issues.failure_explanation: Injectivity of the retained DoFs on \(\mathscr S\) only says that those DoFs identify an element already known to lie in \(\mathscr S\). It does not make the right-hand sides \((\boldsymbol v,\boldsymbol p)\) of the L2-projection equations computable from those DoFs. Two elements of \(\mathbf V\) can have identical retained DoFs but different L2 moments against \(\mathscr S\). Consequently, neither the asserted computability nor the unisolvence of the retained DoFs on the space defined by \(\cref{eqdefvs}\) follows from the stated hypothesis.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of the second identity verifies only the normal-flux moments and zero divergence of the curl. Equality in the face virtual element space also requires its interior curl-related DoFs [3], corresponding to edge-space DoFs [4], but the serendipity edge definition permits those DoFs to be reduced and imposes no commuting relation between the two L2 projections. Likewise, the first identity requires enough boundary moments, such as \(k\ge k_{\mathrm d}\), which the proposition does not assume. The third displayed identity also literally applies curl to a scalar; even after the evident replacement by gradient, the required compatibility of all relevant reduced DoFs and orders is not established.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Let
  \(\left\{\boldsymbol{\psi}_{i}^l\right\},i=1,\dots,N_{S}\) be a set of
  Lagrange bases of \(\mathbf{V}^{\mathrm{S}}_{l}\)

As \(\left\|\bm{\mathit{\Pi}}_{l}\boldsymbol{\psi}^l_{i}\right\|\) monotonically increases with \(l\), it must converges as \(l\rightarrow\infty\). Denote the limit by \(\left\|\bm{\mathit{\Pi}}\boldsymbol{\psi}^\infty_{i}\right\|\). By the density of polynomials, \(\left\|\bm{\mathit{\Pi}}\boldsymbol{\psi}^\infty_{i}\right\|=\left\|\boldsymbol{\psi}^\infty_{i}\right\|\). Since the Lagrange bases are linear independent, there
  must be some \(l\) making \(\mathbf{M}^l\) full row rank.

issues.failure_explanation: Both the space \(\mathbf V_l^{\mathrm S}\) and its Lagrange functions \(\psi_i^l\) vary with \(l\). Therefore their moments against a fixed low-order polynomial need not remain unchanged, the projected norms need not be monotone, and no limiting functions \(\psi_i^\infty\) or convergence to them has been established. Polynomial density applies to each fixed L2 function, not to an uncontrolled sequence of functions from changing spaces. Linear independence at each separate level consequently does not imply that any finite matrix \(M^l\) has full row rank.
